rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2, 2.6, 3.1-3.3 and Tables 3-6 - the study trains and tests SVM, ANN and RVM models on its own six years of lysimeter-derived Kc data for pepper and watermelon under drip and sub-irrigation with plastic mulch, and compares predicted Kc/ETc with lysimeter measurements and FAO-56 values.
rows.notes: The study is a primary modelling study, but it does not test irrigation scheduling or measure any gain in irrigation efficiency or water conservation. Its own result is that an SVM model predicts crop coefficients (Kc) and crop ET from days after transplant, water table depth and rainfall events with lower error than FAO-56 (pepper ETc error 11.2% vs 35.3%; watermelon 2.6% vs 41.7% excluding initial stage) and outperforms ANN and RVM. The statement that improved Kc could help water conservation through better irrigation scheduling (Introduction, Conclusions) is an expectation, not a tested outcome. The study therefore supports only a precondition (more accurate ET estimation) of the claimed efficiency gain, so Q2 is no and upstream is set to true. The 112 ha farm application is an ETc estimation scale-up, not an evaluation of scheduling or water savings.

notes: Full text available and complete. The study concerns machine-learning prediction of crop coefficients from lysimeter data, not a scheduling application or water-saving trial.
